survey.prepared: The town of Quedlinburg's own tourist-office page, read in a search result rather than an extract. It is not a survey and not a register; it is quoted because it is the source of the only stock figure this record carries, and the figure is one four sources disagree about.

quotes.text: In a still largely enclosed, medieval-looking town complex at the foot of the historic castle hill, more than 2000 half-timbered houses have been preserved despite considerable losses in the past decades. Quedlinburg is thus regarded as the largest are monument in Germany.
quotes.page: quedlinburg-info.de, English page for the Fachwerkmuseum im Ständerbau. Not paginated. 'the largest are monument' is the page's own typographical error for 'area monument' and is quoted as printed.

measurements.name: half_timbered_house_count
measurements.as_printed: more than 2000 half-timbered houses have been preserved
measurements.note: A LOWER BOUND ('more than'), and FOUR SOURCES READ ON ONE DAY GIVE FOUR NUMBERS: this page's 'more than 2000'; World Heritage Explorer's 'around 2,100 timber houses'; culturalheritageonline's '1,300 Fachwerk buildings'; and everything-everywhere's 'around 800 houses in the town that are considered as important monuments'. The last is a count of MONUMENTS and not of half-timbered houses, which is probably the whole of that discrepancy, and the 1,300 against 2,100 is not explained by anything read. The figure is carried with its spread stated because a single number here would be a false precision.

note: Tranche 3, Germanic cluster, 5 September 2026. A DISTRICT record and declared as one. Added because the node had four buildings and no account of the population they come from, and because the disagreement about the size of that population -- 800, 1,300, 2,000-plus, 2,100 -- is itself the finding: nobody reading four sources in one afternoon can say within a factor of two how many half-timbered houses stand in the best-preserved half-timbered town in Germany.
